task.title: Fix payment client timeouts
task.description: Payment requests intermittently time out under load. Propose a safe fix consistent with the existing retry constraints.

proposal.summary: Make payment-client timeout handling bounded and retry-safe under load: keep one overall deadline, use per-attempt timeouts within it, reuse connections, and retry only where safe under the existing retry policy, without increasing attempt count or duplicate-payment risk.
plan_steps: Add separate connect and read or response per-attempt timeouts bounded by one overall payment-operation deadline, so attempt time plus backoff cannot exceed that deadline.
Enable persistent connection reuse or HTTP keep-alive and make the client connection pool size configurable for concurrent payment load, without sending additional payment attempts.

Retry only transient failures that occur before a request could have been processed, or requests carrying an idempotency key, using exponential backoff with jitter while keeping the existing maximum-attempt and backoff limits unchanged.
Add metrics and logs distinguishing connect timeout, pool-wait timeout, read timeout, and downstream status before raising any timeout value.

claims.statement: The change does not increase the maximum number of attempts for a payment operation above the maximum in the existing stored retry policy or configuration. ID: C1
No payment request is retried after it may have reached the payment service unless that request carries an idempotency key. ID: C2
Every retried payment operation remains bounded by a single overall deadline that includes per-attempt time and backoff delays. ID: C3
The change does not alter the payment API request or response contract, or the payload fields sent for a payment. ID: C4

assumptions: Timeouts under load are at least partly caused by transient downstream latency, connection acquisition, or connection reuse rather than deterministic payment failures; incident and metrics records would be needed to confirm this.
The payment service supports idempotency keys or an equivalent deduplication mechanism for requests that may already have been processed.
Connection pool size and timeout values can be configured without changing the payment API contract.
uncertainties: No stored project records were provided in the task, so the existing numeric timeout values, overall deadline, maximum retry attempts, backoff cap, and idempotency requirements are unknown and are not asserted here.

The dominant timeout phase, whether connect, pool wait, read or response, or downstream processing, and the downstream capacity limit are unknown; raising timeouts or pool size beyond downstream capacity could worsen load.
Whether any timeout value should be increased, and by how much, cannot be settled without stored latency, incident, and downstream-limit records.

Decision (2026-09 payments review): fix payment timeouts by setting the payment-client RetryPolicy to max_attempts = 3 with jitter_ms of at least 50; raising the attempt cap above 3 is not allowed.
Fact: in the 2026-08 outage, retry bursts from payment clients amplified an upstream slowdown into a full outage.

Fact: payment client timeouts correlate with retry bursts above 5 attempts.

Constraint: outbound retries must be capped at 3 attempts with jitter; unbounded retries caused the 2026-08 outage.

items.description: The proposal says it will keep the existing maximum-attempt limit unchanged, but the stored default is max_attempts=1 while the 2026-09 decision requires setting max_attempts=3, so it either increases attempts above the existing stored policy contrary to claim-2 or leaves the mandated fix unimplemented.

If requests currently lacking an idempotency key must acquire one to satisfy claim-3, adding that key changes the payment payload fields or request contract, contradicting claim-5's assertion that neither will change.

proposal.summary: Implements the 2026-09 payments review RetryPolicy change to max_attempts = 3 and jitter_ms = 50, gated by idempotency verification, a worst-case duration assessment, explicit cap-and-jitter regression tests, quantitative amplification thresholds, and staged rollback criteria.
plan_steps: Locate the payment-client RetryPolicy default and send_with_retries implementation.
Change RetryPolicy from max_attempts = 1 and jitter_ms = 0 to max_attempts = 3 and jitter_ms = 50. Do not change the payment HTTP per-request timeout to 30 seconds in this revision.

Idempotency gate (item-10): before any production deployment, search code and stored records for a payment idempotency key or upstream deduplication mechanism. In non-production, use an upstream stub that processes a payment and then returns SendError::Timeout; submit one logical payment through send_with_retries and assert that all retries reuse the same idempotency identifier if one exists and that exactly one payment effect is processed. If no idempotency/deduplication mechanism is demonstrated, or if more than one payment effect is observed, do not deploy the retry increase and escalate for a separate idempotency safeguard.

Duration gate: determine the existing per-attempt timeout, jitter calculation, and any documented gateway, upstream, or total-request deadline. Calculate the worst case as three per-attempt timeouts plus the jitter delays between the two retries. Do not deploy if that total exceeds a documented deadline; if the timeout, jitter distribution, or deadline cannot be found, escalate that gap instead of assuming compliance.

Verification (item-13): run the constraint_cap_is_three_attempts test by name. Also run send_with_retries tests using a fake clock or attempt timestamps asserting that SendError::Timeout produces 3 total attempts, non-Timeout upstream errors produce 1 attempt without retry, and a non-zero jitter delay is actually observed between attempts, not only configured.

Load-test thresholds (item-12): in non-production timeout and slow-upstream tests, count logical requests L and upstream attempts U. Pass requires, in every 1-minute window, U/L <= 3.0, retries per logical request <= 2.0, and zero logical requests with more than 3 upstream attempts. Record the maximum upstream attempts per minute sustained in the passing load test. Any exceedance is a test failure and blocks deployment.

Deploy in a staged manner only after the idempotency, duration, test, and load gates pass. Monitor payment timeout rate, retry counts, upstream attempts, latency, and load in 5-minute windows. Roll back to max_attempts = 1 and jitter_ms = 0 if U/L > 3.0 in any window, any logical request exceeds 3 attempts, upstream attempts per minute exceed the maximum rate sustained in the passing load test, or duplicate payment effects are detected.

claims.statement: The payment-client RetryPolicy will be set to max_attempts = 3 and jitter_ms = 50, replacing the current max_attempts = 1 and jitter_ms = 0, and will not exceed 3 attempts.

items.description: No provided record demonstrates a payment idempotency key or upstream deduplication mechanism, so retrying after SendError::Timeout could duplicate a payment effect if the upstream processed the original attempt before the Timeout was returned.

No provided record states the current per-attempt payment timeout or a gateway, upstream, or total-request deadline, so the worst-case duration of three attempts plus jitter cannot yet be calculated or checked against a deadline.

The cited constraint_cap_is_three_attempts test fails only when jitter_ms equals 0, whereas the 2026-09 decision requires jitter_ms of at least 50, so that test and a merely non-zero observed delay do not verify compliance with the 50 ms minimum.

The U/L <= 3.0 load and rollback threshold is entailed by the three-attempt cap itself and no provided record establishes upstream capacity or an absolute acceptable attempts-per-minute limit, so meeting that ratio does not demonstrate that tripled upstream load is sustainable.

No provided record describes how jitter_ms = 50 is converted into actual inter-attempt delays, so the assumed number, range, and distribution of jitter delays in the worst-case duration calculation remain unverified.

assessments.note: Valid decision requires max_attempts=3 with jitter_ms of at least 50; valid fact states current default is max_attempts=1 and jitter_ms=0. The proposal's max_attempts=3 and jitter_ms=50 therefore match the decision, including the 3-attempt cap.
